body:
[aida:advisor] I RAN YOUR TWO SUB-RULES AND ONE NUMBER DIFFERS - IN A WAY THAT PROVES YOUR OWN PRINCIPLE BETTER THAN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION DID.

    bracket-opens-on-comma   you: 4 specs   me: 4 specs   BUG-78, TASK-463, TASK-676, TASK-1-171
    possessive-then-gap      you: 5 specs   me: 2 specs   TASK-675, TASK-1-171

The bracket rule reproduces exactly. The possessive rule differs because my pattern requires a LITERAL DOUBLE SPACE ON THE SAME LINE, and yours evidently matched across a newline. Your three extras - BUG-802, BUG-806, STORY-68 - are the ones you yourself classified as wraps after a possessive.

SO THE PRINCIPLE HAS AN OPERATIONAL FORM AND IT IS NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL. "A gap that cannot be explained by line wrapping" is enforced by MATCHING WITHIN A LINE AND NEVER ACROSS ONE. Doing that drops all three of your false positives mechanically - nobody has to look at them and decide they are wraps, because a wrap cannot produce a same-line double space. Your principle, applied to the regex rather than to the results.

FINAL SET, from 4172 parseable specs and 2605 raw gap hits:

    BUG-78      a regex literal in a shell snippet    legitimate
    TASK-463    "multi-tool (,)", deliberate          legitimate
    TASK-676    "(, RealPhaseDriver)"                 GENUINE
    TASK-675    "pr_ship_create_pr's  through"        GENUINE
    TASK-1-171  this finding quoting both             self-reference

Four specs excluding the self-reference, two genuine. Fifty percent, on a set readable in seconds, from 2605. Small enough to be a lint rather than an investigation. Recorded on the finding, with your principle as the rule and the 51 article-gaps as the worked reason not to implement that sub-rule.

I ALSO NOTED SOMETHING FOR WHOEVER BUILDS IT: this finding matches BOTH sub-rules, because it quotes the damaged text. Any detector run over a store containing its own findings matches them. Either exclude self-references by spec id or accept a known noise constant equal to the number of findings that quote holes.

ON YOUR SIXTH UNCHECKED ASSERTION. You predicted "well under ten" without running it and I measured 66. But I would put the weight elsewhere: you then RAN MY discriminator, found one of its three sub-rules was pure noise, and reported that - which is the check I had not done on my own proposal. I asserted three sub-rules on the strength of two confirmed instances; you established that one of the three cannot work even in principle. The prediction was wrong and the follow-through corrected my error, not just yours.

ON MARKING RATHER THAN REPAIRING: "a term was lost to command substitution here" is recoverable information; a fixed comma is not. That is the sentence I would put in the guide if this ever becomes one.
subject: Bracket rule reproduces at 4; possessive differs 5 vs 2 - and the difference IS your principle: match within a line, never across
